description: Incident ledger used by scripts/alert-audit.mjs. One entry per real incident or game-day, sourced from docs/postmortems/, docs/game-days/ and the Upptime history in history/. Add an entry after every postmortem; the audit is only as good as this list.

incidents.summary: oracle-service cached malformed verification payloads after an upstream schema change; the frontend rendered VERIFICATION FAILED badges while every service reported healthy.

coverageGap.reason: The service answered 200 with a well-formed-but-wrong payload; no metric distinguishes a schema-invalid verdict from a valid one. Tracked as a follow-up: emit oracle_verification_outcome_total{outcome="rejected-invalid-payload"} from the cache reader added in the hotfix, then add a rule on it.

incidents.summary: Upptime recorded indexer.iln.finance/health down for 2 minutes.
Upptime recorded the notifications health endpoint down for 2 minutes.

Upptime recorded oracle.iln.finance/v1/health down continuously for five days (0.00% monthly uptime). No Prometheus alert fired: every oracle rule is a ratio over request counters, which stay at zero when nothing reaches the service.

service-down.description: A scrape target stopped answering. Ratio-based SLO rules cannot fire here because their denominators are zero.

oracle-verdict-integrity.description: The oracle answers successfully with verdicts that are wrong or unparseable.

indexer-lag.description: The indexer cursor stops advancing (docs/monitoring.md, Signal 2).

notifications-degraded.description: Notifications are being delivered through fallback providers.

OracleVerificationLatencyHigh.reason: Static p95 > 2s duplicate of OracleLatencyFastBurn (SLO threshold 1s). Fired for the 2026-08-30 game-day as OracleServiceLatencyHigh only in the incident narrative; the burn-rate rule covers the same signal with the SLO's own threshold, so one paging rule per symptom.

OracleStaleResponsesRising.reason: rate(oracle_stale_responses_total[10m]) > 0 pages on a single stale verdict in ten minutes. Never corresponded to an incident; OracleFreshnessFastBurn/SlowBurn alert on the stale ratio against the 99.5% SLO instead.

OracleNoVerifications.reason: Kept as the only rule that catches a silently idle oracle, but 15 minutes of no traffic is normal outside business hours on testnet. Window widened to 30m so it fires on an outage, not a quiet evening.

OracleCacheHitRateLow.reason: Documented to be noisy right after deploys and Redis restarts. for: raised from 15m to 30m.

ServiceDown.reason: Three of the four recorded incidents were plain unavailability that no existing rule could fire on.

IndexerCursorStale.reason: docs/monitoring.md Signal 2 specifies syncLag > 60s warning and > 300s critical, but no Prometheus rule implemented it; iln_cursor_updated_at is already exported.

IndexerCursorStaleCritical.reason: Critical tier of the same signal.

NotificationsFallbackActive.reason: Fallback deliveries are the degraded-mode signal called out in NotificationDeliveryFastBurn's own annotation but had no rule.

IndexerDatabaseErrors.reason: Signal 2 lists db: error as critical; iln_db_errors_total existed with no rule.
